job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: This role is located in New York City and will require a hybrid work schedule of at least 2 days in office per week

Information Risk Governance (“IRG”) provides oversight to information and cyber security risk by maintaining and improving branch wide framework that is in-line with the Head Office and regulatory requirements and addresses Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability for information assets

IRG establishes appropriate policies, procedures, measurement, and monitoring processes to proactively assess and evaluate and cyber security and information security risks inherent in the Branch Operations
IRG is directly involved in all information and cyber security related projects, matters and issues
The Information Security Risk Analyst is responsible for supporting the organization’s vulnerability management program and performing assigned information security risk assessments

This role will perform the day-to-day vulnerability management activities, perform risk-based analysis of identified vulnerabilities, coordinate remediation efforts with the IT Department, and help ensure systems are maintained in accordance with the organization’s information security standards
Administer and support the organization’s system vulnerability management program
Conduct regular vulnerability scans across servers, endpoints, applications, network infrastructure, and Cloud environments

Monitor vulnerability scanning coverage and coordinate with the IT Department to identify missing, newly added, or decommissioned IT assets and ensure that the scanning scope remains accurate and up to date
Review and analyze vulnerability scan results and cross-reference with other sources such as the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to identify high-criticality areas for remediation
Identify potential false-positive findings and review with ITD for validity
Collaborate with ITD to prioritize system vulnerability remediation and patching based on system risk severity, vulnerability exploitability, asset criticality, and potential business impact

Track identified vulnerabilities through remediation and/or mitigation, validate remediation through re-scanning or review of appropriate supporting evidence, and generate regular system vulnerability remediation status reports
Monitor compliance of system vulnerability remediation based on pre-defined risk-based remediation targets
Escalate critical or significant delays of system vulnerability remediation based on pre-defined targets to Management, as necessary
Create vulnerability management-related reports with risk summaries and recommendations to Management
Perform risk assessments on proposed new systems to be introduced to the organization
Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by management

Basic Purpose: This role supports the Security Second Line of Defense (2LOD) Issue Management function by providing independent oversight, effective challenge, quality assurance, and issue lifecycle governance for security issues.   •    Review and challenge corrective action plans for adequacy, sustainability, and root cause alignment.

  •    Validate issue closure packages and remediation evidence.

  •    Keep current with Information Security best practices and industry trends, communicate these practices to relevant stakeholders.

  •    Perform other duties as assigned. 

Qualifications

  •    Experience in the credit union/financial services industry with a focus on regulatory frameworks, information security assessments, and remediation activities 

  •    Desired knowledge of NCUA, FFIEC, GLBA, NIST (including the Cyber Security Framework and 800 Series 

  •    Demonstrated knowledge of Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) programs.

  •    Understanding of the Three Lines Model and Security Second Line of Defense responsibilities.

  •    Experience performing independent challenge and oversight functions.

  •    Knowledge of NCUA, FFIEC, NIST (including Cyber Security Framework and 800 Series controls)

  •    Working knowledge of Vulnerability Management, Identity and Access Management, Network Security, Cloud Security and Data protection controls

  •    Strong planning and organizational skills

  •    Strong analytical skills (root cause analysis, risk assessment, etc)

  •    Strong verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills, including technical writing

  •    Experience working with all levels of staff, management, stakeholders and 3rd parties

  •    Desired bachelor's degree in business, information systems or related field or equivalent work/military experience

job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: The Senior Credit Risk Analyst is responsible for evaluating and managing customer credit risk across Vertiv's Americas business while supporting revenue growth, cash flow protection, and compliance with company policies

This role performs financial and credit analysis for new and existing customers, establishes and monitors credit limits, reviews complex commercial transactions, and recommends strategies to mitigate financial risk

The Senior Credit Risk Analyst serves as a key business partner to Sales, Order Management, Legal, Finance, Collections, and executive leadership by providing timely and well-supported credit decisions that balance risk and business objectives

Identify, recommend, and participate in initiatives that improve credit processes, workflow efficiency, system utilization, reporting capabilities, automation, and overall operational excellence
Assist with documenting and updating standard operating procedures and training materials
Manage and support ad hoc projects, reporting requests, and business initiatives as assigned

jobs_results.description:
POSITION SUMMARY


Vertiv, a global leader in critical infrastructure solutions, seeks a Sr. Credit Risk Analyst at its Headquarters in Westerville, Ohio to join our Americas Finance team.


The Senior Credit Risk Analyst is responsible for evaluating and managing customer credit risk across Vertiv's Americas business while supporting revenue growth, cash flow protection, and compliance with company policies. This role performs financial and credit analysis for new and existing customers, establishes and monitors credit limits, reviews complex commercial transactions, and recommends strategies to mitigate financial risk.


The Senior Credit Risk Analyst serves as a key business partner to Sales, Order Management, Legal, Finance, Collections, and executive leadership by providing timely and well-supported credit decisions that balance risk and business objectives. The role also supports process improvement initiatives, SOX compliance activities, credit hold management, portfolio monitoring, and reporting for management and audit purposes.


Additionally, the Senior Credit Risk Analyst maintains delegated credit approval authority up to $1,000,000 and provides recommendations for transactions requiring higher levels of approval.


PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES



 Conduct comprehensive credit reviews for new and existing customers, including analysis of audited and unaudited financial statements, credit applications, trade references, bank references, credit bureau reports, and publicly available information.
 Establish appropriate credit limits and risk mitigation requirements based on financial strength, payment history, business outlook, and project exposure.
 Evaluate large-scale project opportunities where future exposure may significantly exceed approved credit limits.
 Conduct recurring customer portfolio reviews to ensure credit limits remain aligned with current business activity and financial condition.

 Experience in a manufacturing, construction or industrial environment preferred.
